- Focus your tree practice on **Binary Trees** and **Binary Search Trees (BST)**. These make up roughly 90% of interview questions on LeetCode and HackerRank. Questions usually ask you to traverse, search, or modify the tree using recursion. [](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/connerardman_studying-for-coding-interviews-doesnt-need-activity-7316452468496707584-KXCJ)
- ![](data:image/png;base64,)LinkedIn·Conner Ardman +4
- 🌳 Which Trees to Know
	- **Binary Tree:** A tree where every node has at most two children. You must know these traversals perfectly:
		- **Pre-Order:** Visit Root → Left → Right.
		- **In-Order:** Visit Left → Root → Right (perfect for getting a sorted list from a BST).
		- **Post-Order:** Visit Left → Right → Root (used for deletion and bottom-up calculations). [](https://www.techinterviewhandbook.org/algorithms/tree/)
			- ![](data:image/png;base64,)Tech Interview Handbook +4
	- **Binary Search Tree (BST):** A special binary tree where everything to the left is smaller, and everything to the right is larger.
	- **Prefix Tree (Trie):** Used heavily for solving autocomplete and word-matching questions. [](https://www.quora.com/What-algorithms-should-I-know-to-crack-my-coding-interview-for-an-entry-level-full-stack)
		- ![](data:image/png;base64,)Quora +3

- 📊 Platform Breakdown & Patterns
- Platforms like GeeksforGeeks and LeetCode divide problems into three levels: [](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/top-50-tree-coding-problems-for-interviews/)
- ![](data:image/png;base64,)GeeksforGeeks
	- **Easy:** Find the maximum height of a tree, check if two trees are identical, or check if a tree is balanced. (Time: O(n), Space: O(h)).
	- **Medium:** Find the diameter of a tree (the longest path between any two nodes), find the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA), or print the tree level by level. These require **Breadth-First Search (BFS)** or advanced depth tricks.
	- **Hard:** Reconstruct a tree given its traversal lists, or find the maximum path between any two leaf nodes. [](https://leetcode.com/discuss/study-guide/3733791/Top-50-Tree-Coding-Problems-for-Interviews/)
		- ![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)LeetCode +4
- 💡 The Big Secret: How to Solve Them
- Master the recursive "pattern." Imagine a tree as smaller trees stacked on top of each other. If you know how to solve a problem for the top node (the Root), you can tell the computer to do the exact same thing for all the nodes below it! To start practicing, filter LeetCode by the "Tree" tag and try easy problems first. [](https://leetcode.com/discuss/career/5072269/All-Trees-Questions/)
